No more manual deploys, forgotten tests, or 2 a.m. panic patches — here’s how one serverless function and a handful of YAML files quietly took over my job
The Problem: Death by a Thousand Manual Steps
Six months ago, shipping a single feature meant running through a mental checklist that lived nowhere except my own head:

• Run the tests locally (if I remembered)

• Lint the code (if I remembered)

• Bump the version number

• Build the project

• Deploy manually via CLI

• Post an update in the team channel

• Clean up the old preview environment from last week that I definitely forgot about
Every step was a chance to skip something, fat-finger a command, or deploy code that quietly broke staging while I was making coffee. None of it was hard. All of it was tedious. And tedious work is exactly the kind of work that eventually gets skipped under deadline pressure — which is how bugs sneak into production.
